bull_bear.body: Disciplined brownfield-heavy expansion; Net cash balance sheet supports M&A closure; Focus on ROCE improvement (up 180bps to 22.8% ex-Kasargod).
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Regulatory delay in NCLT merger approval; Geopolitical impact on MVT (UAE/Middle East); Competition for clinical talent in metros; Execution risk on large bed-addition pipeline.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident and execution-focused; Emphasizes 'disciplined growth' and 'clinical excellence'; Transparent on nurse strike resolution and MVT diversification success.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Diagnostics segment has fully turned around (12.8% margin) becoming a profit contributor rather than a drag; MVT diversification to Maldives/Africa successfully neutralized UAE macro headwinds within a single quarter; Nurse strike settlement cost was significantly lower than market fears (INR 40k demand vs actual ~INR 3.5k-4k increment).
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Proforma Q1FY27 net debt is shown as Aster (511), Quality Care 1,162 and Merged Entity 1,673 (INR Cr) — the deck prints these three figures without reconciling them to each other.
- Aster's CWIP for ongoing projects (including ROU, capital advances and capital creditors) is INR 1,238 Cr for Q1 FY27 versus INR 1,057 Cr in Q1 FY26.
- Returns framed as improving on better asset utilisation: combined RoCE of 22.9% in Q1FY27 vs 20.4% (+246 bps), computed on average capital employed excluding revaluation reserves, CWIP and intangibles.
- "CAPEX Efficiencies" is an explicit synergy lever, and the bed plan leans 53% on existing facilities rather than new builds.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body: Hospitals: Rev +17% (ex-Kasargod), EBITDA +31%; MVT: +41% YoY (Kerala +51%); Labs: Rev +18%, EBITDA margin expanded to 12.8% (from -7.6% in FY24); Clusters: Kerala (EBITDA margin 25.6%), K&M (24.5%), A&T (18.3%, +700bps expansion).
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Consolidation of two major hospital chains creating a dominant pan-India platform with enhanced pricing power and operational synergies. | Aster DM Healthcare Ltd | beneficiary | High | Merger with QCIL adds scale, diversifies geography (strong South India presence), and accelerates margin expansion through best-practice sharing. |
| Increased competition for market share and clinical talent in key southern markets due to the creation of a larger rival entity. | Regional Hospital Peers | loser | Med | Smaller regional players may face pressure on empanelment rates and doctor retention as the merged entity leverages scale. |
business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- Merger became effective on July 1, 2026 forming Aster DM Quality Care Limited, described as "Executed on schedule with zero operational friction" across 41+ sites with zero service disruption.
- Stated merger rationale has six planks: Scale ("one of the top 3 hospital chains in India"), Enhanced Metrics, Synergies, Diversification ("low overlap in cities of presence"), in-built Growth Potential for brownfield and greenfield expansion, and "Backing of Global Marquee Investor" Blackstone.
- Combined footprint of 39 hospitals, 9 states, 28 cities, 321 labs & PECs and 205 pharmacies (pharmacies in India operated by ARPPL under brand license from Aster), with 37,700+ workforce and 7,400+ doctors.
- Geographic skew stated as 35% Metro and Tier 1 / 65% Tier 2 & Tier 3 cities.
- Clinical differentiation claimed through firsts and rankings: Kerala's 1st transcatheter Fontan procedure, Karnataka's 1st robotic-assisted revision knee replacement (CORI), India's 1st and largest Robotic Hepatic Artery Infusion therapy, and four Aster hospitals in Newsweek's 2026 World's Best Hospital Rankings.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Merger] The listed entity has been renamed — the covering letter is signed "For Aster DM Quality Care Limited (Formerly Aster DM Healthcare Limited)"; the merger became effective July 1, 2026.
- [Proforma caveat] The deck repeatedly warns that "Quality Care numbers are indicative and subject to statutory audit adjustments" and that "Proforma numbers for combined entity are also subject to finalization and audit of the merged accounts", with actual amounts potentially differing materially, including from harmonization of accounting policies.
- [Cultural integration] A structured integration programme covering 41+ sites, 4,000+ key leaders aligned via a day-1 leadership webinar and 45,000+ celebration kits delivered, under the "#GO GREATER" single brand and operating framework.
- [Exceptional cost] Aster's Normalised PAT for Q1 FY27 excludes exceptional merger-related expenses of INR 114.4 Cr (Q1 FY26: INR 4.4 Cr).
- [Accreditation] "CARE Hitech secured JCI accreditation, becoming the 1st unit in CARE network"; Quality Care onboarded 50+ doctors contributing ~9.5 Cr in monthly revenue.
- [Leadership] Varun Khanna is Managing Director and Group CEO, Dr Azad Moopen Executive Chairman, Alisha Moopen Executive Director and Sunil Kumar M R Group CFO.
business.title: Notable from the deck

deepdive.thesis: Aster DM delivered robust Q4FY26 growth (Rev +18%, EBITDA +26%) driven by volume recovery and higher-acuity mix, while the imminent merger with QCIL creates a pan-India giant (>15k beds) with significant synergy potential. The resolution of the Kerala nurse strike with minimal financial impact (INR 5-6cr) and a successful turnaround in diagnostics remove key overhangs, positioning the combined entity for sustained double-digit earnings growth.

open.item: Major GIPSA (Bangalore) insurance contract to be renewed in H2FY26, expected to give a considerable ARPOB increase.
QCIL merger received 96.7% shareholder approval plus creditor approval; matter before NCLT with next hearing expected in May, and completion expected within Q1FY27.
13 MW of renewable-energy projects commissioned across 3 hospitals; on track to add another 21 MW across 7 more hospitals in H2FY26 and early FY27.

K&M cluster IP volume (soft at 3%, ~ -8% at Aster Aadhar due to scheme de-empanelment) expected to recover to mid-to-high single digit over the next one to two quarters as newly hired doctors stabilize.
Kasargod hospital (FY26 loss ~INR 19-20 cr, ~60 bps margin drag) expected to break even in a quarter or two.
Aster Capital Trivandrum expected to commence around October 2026 (H2FY27 beginning), leveraging the QCIL/KIMS network in an under-penetrated market; limited EBITDA dilution expected.
Management expects Aster's EBITDA margin to grow year-on-year with no dilution despite new capacity, aided by EBITDA-accretive brownfield adds and post-merger synergies.
QCIL, currently under-leveraged in oncology, expects significant growth in oncology volumes over the next two years to drive CONGO-T mix (58-59%) toward mid-60s.
Bengaluru expansion runway intact: Sarjapur hospital to commence in ~one more year and Yeswanthpur in ~three more years, alongside spare occupancy at CMI/RV/Whitefield.
Combined capacity of 10,620+ beds across 28 cities, with a pipeline of 4,445 additional beds to take total capacity beyond 15,000 beds via greenfield and brownfield expansion.
Aster to add ~2,500 beds over the next four years at a cost of INR 2,700 cr (INR 350 cr invested to March 2026), taking total capacity to over 8,150 beds.
QCIL to invest ~INR 2,000 cr to add over 1,700 beds in the next 3-4 years (~1,300 non-metro), of which ~1,500 brownfield and ~200 greenfield.
Planned Kerala brownfield expansions of 150 beds at MIMS Calicut and 130 beds at MIMS Kannur, part of Kerala's 800+ bed pipeline.

Aster-QCIL merger synergies (procurement, etc.) not yet started; expected to begin flowing from day one post-merger (targeted from Q1FY27), on top of QCIL's internal INR 85 cr procurement synergies already realized in FY26.
Blended CONGO case mix (now 55%) targeted to rise to 60% and then 65%, providing headroom for acuity and ARPOB improvement.
Bengaluru cluster ARPOB (~INR 77,000, mature ~75,000) has headroom to grow another ~6-7% as CONGO-T/oncology mix rises.
Corporate headquarters being shifted from Bangalore to Hyderabad so the NCLT merger application proceeds from a single state for more efficient process timelines.
GST rate reduction expected to cut ~1.1% of monthly top line (~35-40 bps EBITDA hit), largely offset by the ~INR 2 cr/month positive revenue impact from the October CGHS price increase.
Integrate diagnostics, pharmacy and home care into the Aster Health app (now 100,000+ downloads, first Malayalam regional-language health super app) to create an end-to-end ecosystem.
Effective tax rate near 30% expected to continue as carry-forward losses are largely utilized.
